traceability.notes:
All key acceptance criteria and story requirements for 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS are implemented and verified:
- Core Functionality: The require-branch-annotation rule exists, is registered in the plugin, and, per tests, detects missing @story and/or @req on all specified significant branch types (if, switch cases including special-case/default handling, try/finally, catch, and all loop forms). It also provides auto-fixes for missing annotations where appropriate. - Quality Standards: The rule is implemented as a standard ESLint RuleModule with proper meta, schema, message definitions, and uses helper utilities for configuration validation and comment/annotation parsing. Tests use RuleTester in line with ESLint best practices. - Integration: The rule relies on ESLint’s AST traversal, so nested branches are handled naturally; each branch node—regardless of nesting level—gets its own visitor and annotation check. The default and configurable branchTypes define the scope of enforcement and are verified by unit tests. - User Experience: Error messages use a clear, parameterized messageId (missingAnnotation) that tells the user exactly which annotation (@story or @req) is missing, and ESLint’s usual location reporting indicates which branch needs it. Auto-fix inserts template annotations in the correct place and with correct indentation. - Error Handling: Misconfiguration of branchTypes is handled gracefully by validateBranchTypes, which returns a Program listener that reports explicit configuration errors for each invalid type. The rule also deliberately allows certain benign patterns (e.g., switch default without annotations) as covered by tests. - Documentation: A dedicated rule doc describes behavior, options, and examples (correct, incorrect, and invalid configuration), and the README points to this rule. Implementation files and tests are annotated with this story and requirement IDs, ensuring traceability.
There is no evidence of missing core behavior relative to the story’s requirements (branch detection, comment association, annotation parsing, significance criteria via DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES, configurable scope, and an efficient, linear scan implementation). All related tests pass in the full test suite, so this story is assessed as fully implemented.
